findings.claim: subscribe(), unsubscribe(), and _schedule_resource_update_notifications() access self._subscribers without holding any lock. The self._snapshot_lock introduced at __init__ guards only self._snapshot; no corresponding _subscribers_lock was added in fr4.
findings.evidence: resources.py:453: self._snapshot_lock = threading.Lock() — no _subscribers_lock present in __init__. resources.py:480–481: subscribe() calls self._subscribers.setdefault(uri, set()).add(session) — two non-atomic operations without a lock. resources.py:483–488: unsubscribe() reads the uri bucket, conditionally discards, and conditionally pops — three non-atomic steps. resources.py:552–558: _schedule_resource_update_notifications() takes list() snapshots of .items() and each sessions set, partially mitigating mid-iteration mutation, but no lock prevents a concurrent subscribe() from adding a session that is missed by the list() snapshot or a concurrent unsubscribe() from emptying a set whose reference was captured before the discard.
findings.impact: In the current stdio transport the asyncio event loop serialises session callbacks so the race window is negligible and no crash path is reachable in practice. In the 021H HTTP transport with concurrent connections, the check-then-act hazard in unsubscribe() and the non-atomic setdefault+add in subscribe() could cause a missed resource-update notification (stale client cache until next poll on commit) or a duplicate notification. No data corruption or crash; worst-case effect is a stale MCP client re-polling on the next commit.
findings.mitigation: Add self._subscribers_lock = threading.Lock() at __init__ alongside self._snapshot_lock. Acquire it in subscribe(), unsubscribe(), and around the dict/set read-modify-write sections of _schedule_resource_update_notifications(). The lock need not be held during the async loop.create_task() calls — only during dict and set mutations.

findings.claim: The fr4 fix correctly widened the except clause to catch subprocess.TimeoutExpired and OSError, but test_signing_keys_outage.py was not updated: no regression test exercises either of these two newly-covered degradation paths. The C-R4-001 mitigation explicitly called for a test that patches _git_stdout to raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired and asserts snapshot().key_id is None, the signing-keys error field contains the timeout message, caplog contains 'degrading MCP resource snapshot: signing-keys unavailable', and all other static and per-ID resources remain accessible with key_id=None.
findings.evidence: tests/scp_mcp/test_resources/test_signing_keys_outage.py:1–74: exactly two tests present. test_snapshot_degrades_when_committed_signing_keys_are_malformed (lines 10–48) commits two current=true keys and exercises the RuntimeError('multiple current signing keys declared') path via _parse_signing_keys. test_snapshot_logs_and_degrades_for_empty_committed_signing_keyring (lines 51–74) commits an empty keyring and exercises the RuntimeError('contains no ssh-ed25519 key entries') guard at resources.py:571–574. Neither test patches _git_stdout, _read_committed_text, or subprocess.run to raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired or FileNotFoundError/OSError. The broadened except tuple at resources.py:581 is not exercised by any test for the two newly-added exception classes.
findings.mitigation: Add a third test to test_signing_keys_outage.py that monkeypatches standards_control_plane.mcp_server.resources._git_stdout to raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired('git show', 30) when the signing-keys path is encountered. Assert: catalog.snapshot().key_id is None; catalog.read_static('scp://security/signing-keys')['error'] contains a timeout-related substring; caplog at ERROR level contains 'degrading MCP resource snapshot: signing-keys unavailable'; every URI in STATIC_RESOURCE_URIS returns key_id=None; catalog.read_rule('GOV-001')['key_id'] is None. Optionally add a parallel test for OSError (e.g. FileNotFoundError to simulate absent git binary) following the same assertion pattern.

structured_review.summary: R5 correctness review of slice 021D after fr4. The sole R4 MAJ carry-forward (C-R4-001: subprocess.TimeoutExpired and OSError escaping the signing-keys degradation handler) is confirmed closed: resources.py:581 now reads 'except (RuntimeError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as error:' with an inline comment documenting all three exception classes and the invariant they protect. signing_keys_body is guaranteed to be bound on every exit path of the try/except block, closing the NameError/all-resources-dark failure mode. Two MIN findings remain open: C-R4-002 (carry-forward: subscribe/unsubscribe access self._subscribers without a lock) and C-R5-001 (new: no regression test added for the subprocess.TimeoutExpired or OSError degradation paths, despite being explicitly required by C-R4-001's mitigation). No new MAJ findings. Fixpoint reached per §4.3: APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS (MIN/nit-only).

verified_closures.note: resources.py:581 except clause reads 'except (RuntimeError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as error:'. The inline comment at lines 582–587 enumerates all three exception classes and states the protected invariant ('a malformed/unreadable signing-keys file does NOT take all 11 resource URIs offline'). Note on the inheritance chain: subprocess.TimeoutExpired inherits from subprocess.SubprocessError → Exception (NOT via OSError), so listing it explicitly in the tuple is the correct and necessary approach — it would NOT have been caught by 'except OSError' alone. signing_keys_body is assigned either in the try block (line 570, success path) or in the except block (line 589, degradation path) and is therefore bound at the entry to line 591 (_build_registry call) on all reachable paths. The specific NameError-on-unbound-variable and subsequent repeated-timeout storm are closed. The two pre-existing RuntimeError outage regression tests in test_signing_keys_outage.py remain intact and confirm the original degradation paths are unaffected.
